claim: ERS-010 and ERS-011 state directly contradictory conclusions about the same continuation 4 measurement: ERS-010 grounds the single-strong-model rule in review models differing in depth rather than in kind, and ERS-011 concludes the opposite one unit later. The new owner document would land carrying both.
evidence: ERS-010 canonical_text: "because on identical inputs review models differ in depth rather than in kind and a turn-capped arm reports a ceiling, not a judgement". ERS-011 canonical_text: "and one of the three, at 0.82 dollars, held three findings no other review arm reached, so the review arms differ in depth and, at the margin, in kind".
suggested_repair: Qualify ERS-010 to say the turn-capped comparison showed a depth difference (a proper subset) while separate cheap arms showed marginal kind differences, so both units state one rule.

claim: ERS-008 makes a retained unresolved charge count against the lifetime cap at every admission unconditionally, while ERS-009 and SSYS-037 make blocking-versus-visible-only a user-set disposition. Only the unconditional behaviour is in the cited evidence, so the visible_only option is also a bound the campaign did not exercise and it is not routed through a product-choice packet under ERS-007.
evidence: ERS-008 canonical_text: "retains its cold allowance as a separate unresolved charge that counts against the cap indefinitely"; ERS-008 acceptance: "Admission compares captured usage plus in-flight allowance plus unresolved charges against the lifetime cap before every model request." ERS-009: "and whether unresolved usage blocks further admission or only stays visible"; SSYS-037: "an unresolved-usage disposition of blocks_admission or visible_only". evidence.md attributes to gate/README.md only "Admission against captured usage plus allowances plus unresolved charges" and to cost-policy.json only a "retained unresolved charge" - neither establishes a selectable disposition.
suggested_repair: Make ERS-008 say the unresolved charge counts against the cap when the disposition is blocks_admission and is reported but not deducted when it is visible_only, and record visible_only as a product choice the campaign did not exercise.

claim: The authorization's headline condition and the owner atom's fourth negative constraint are carried by no unit. No unit forbids promising what the September 2026 campaign did not exercise, and no unit states the rule that every promise cites the run that established it; only ERS-012 has a run-naming acceptance criterion.
evidence: authorization.md: "The authorization is explicit that nothing may be promised that the experiments did not exercise, and that every promise cites the run that established it." atom-external-research-owner-canon negative_constraints: "Do not promise a stage, bound or figure the September 2026 campaign did not exercise." Searching all fourteen ERS units plus ACD-467, ATS-054, PLS-023 and SSYS-037: the words "exercise" and "campaign" appear nowhere, and only ERS-012 carries "Reported latency figures name the run that produced them". ERS-010 and ERS-011 name continuation 4 in prose but state no such rule.
suggested_repair: Add the atom's negative constraint verbatim to ERS-001 and an acceptance criterion there that every measured figure in this owner names the run that established it.

claim: The contract-family atom's third negative constraint, which bounds the scripts edit to registration only, is not carried into ATS-054. The unit records the registration and the cardinality bump but never forbids any other change to the verifier, which is the constraint both the authorization and dec-002 relied on.
evidence: atom-external-research-contract-family negative_constraints includes "Do not change any behaviour of the contracts verifier beyond registering this pair." ATS-054 negative_constraints are only: "Do not infer runtime, provider, recovery, security, visual or performance results from fixture validation.", "Do not add schemas or fixture pairs to the gate through an ambient glob.", "Do not convert static validation into execution evidence or a readiness unlock." authorization.md: "as a registration-only scripts edit".
suggested_repair: Add "Do not change any behaviour of scripts/pm-new-contracts-verify.py beyond registering this pair" to ATS-054's negative_constraints.

claim: Plans/Automated_Testing_System.md is edited by this compile but is named by no item of the authorization's enumerated scope, and by no decision record. dec-002 authorizes materializing the contracts pair and registering it in the verifier, not appending a PlanUnit to the testing owner.
evidence: authorization.md scope list: "one owner document Plans/External_Research.md"; "one contracts pair ... added to the contracts verifier's pack list"; "consumer references in Plans/assistant-chat-design.md, Plans/Planning_Ledger_System.md and Plans/Settings_System.md"; "this ledger". compile_queue.json compiled_owner_docs nevertheless lists Plans/Automated_Testing_System.md, and queue-002 compiles ATS-054 into it. dec-002 summary mentions only the schema, fixtures and CONTRACT_PAIRS registration.

claim: ERS-011's measured basis does the two things ERS-010's negative constraints forbid: it compares captured cost across review arms without stating that they ran under the same response ceiling, and it reports four recall figures with no admitted-lead count. It also calls "uncapped" the same arm ERS-010 describes as running at a 160-response ceiling.
evidence: ERS-010 negative_constraints: "Do not compare cost or duration across arms that ran under different ceilings." and "Do not report recall without the admitted-lead count that bounded it." ERS-011 canonical_text: "three cheap review arms reached 34, 36 and 40 of the 110-finding union for 0.53, 0.82 and 0.16 US dollars of captured usage, against 82.52 dollars for the uncapped strong arm's 45". ERS-010 canonical_text calls the same 45-finding arm "its own control - identical inputs, model, effort, admissions, workers and batching at a 160-response ceiling".
suggested_repair: State the response ceiling each arm in ERS-011 ran under and the admitted-lead count behind each recall figure, and use one name for the 45-finding arm across ERS-010 and ERS-011.

suggested_repair: Restore "under the standing repair authorization" to PLS-023's canonical text and add "ledger question record" to its declared tokens.

evidence: ERS-002 declares "reconcile" and "compare" but writes "reconciliation" and "comparison"; ERS-004 declares the atom token "unsupported or already-covered" but writes "unsupported_or_covered" and "unsupported-or-covered"; ERS-007 declares "accepted for planning" and "unapproved optional capability" and writes "authorizes planning it as PlanUnits" and "a deferred or unapproved item"; ERS-008 declares "native records" and writes "native usage records"; ERS-009 declares "bound_by" and writes "names the limit that bound it"; ERS-013 declares "same family" and writes "shares a model family"; ERS-014 declares the atom token "protocol fingerprint" and "output manifest" and writes "two runs sharing a fingerprint" and "a SHA-256 manifest".

claim: ERS-012 requires every stage to report three quantities, then presents its own measured basis as one unlabelled figure per stage. The five figures reconcile with neither the stated wall time nor the stated concurrency, so a reader cannot tell which of the three the unit's own example reports.
evidence: ERS-012 acceptance: "Every stage reports wall span, summed job time including retries, and average concurrency". Its canonical_text then gives "6,378.3 seconds of wall time ... at an average concurrency of 2.620, with discovery 595.1 s, implementation 1,889.2 s, history 2,079.6 s, reconcile 3,699.3 s and compare 658.3 s". Those five sum to 8,921.5 s, which is neither the 6,378.3 s wall nor the 16,711 s that wall x concurrency 2.620 implies.
suggested_repair: Label the per-stage figures as wall spans or as summed job time, and give the missing two quantities for at least the run total.
